project.title: 九月九日忆山东兄弟·王维
project.style_lock:
Match the supplied Chinese diary-comic reference family closely: a clean pure-white digital page, blunt uneven black felt-tip outlines with visible hand wobble, naïve simplified anatomy, and dry wax-colored-pencil fills made from overlapping short diagonal scribbles that deliberately leave small white gaps. Keep the drawing human and slightly clumsy, never polished or vector-perfect.

Use oversized rounded heads, short compact bodies, simple mitten-like hands, dot or short-stroke eyes, tiny noses, expressive eyebrows and mouths, light peach pencil on faces, soft pink cheek marks, and sparse gray pencil strokes for elderly hair. Let posture and gesture carry the emotion; keep violence non-graphic and restrained.

Stage one immediately readable tableau with only the people and props needed for the current beat. Use sparse but recognizable domestic, street, school, or clinic objects drawn with the same rough black contour. Keep most of the background unfilled white. The subject group should usually occupy about 70–82% of the illustration panel while remaining fully inside the safe border; use a medium or wider view by default and a fully contained medium close-up only for a reaction beat.

Limit color to a small muted pencil palette led by dusty hospital blue, brick red, charcoal gray-black, warm beige, pale tan, muted yellow, light gray, and rare muted olive when the scene needs it. Use solid black scribbles for hair, trousers, and the darkest accents. Do not use smooth digital fills, airbrush shading, gradients, glossy highlights, watercolor washes, realistic light, paper grain, manga/anime rendering, 3D, photorealism, decorative borders, logos, signatures, or watermarks.

Treat the approved output board as the final execution target for line weight, pencil density, figure scale, facial simplicity, negative space, and overall finish. Use it to resolve ambiguity between the technique boards and the written description, while ignoring its specific people, actions, and objects.
